This is Siddhartha. Two thousand five hundred years ago, he was born a prince in the Himalayan foothills.
His father wanted him to be king, so he kept him in the palace, away from anything sad.
At twenty-nine, he finally stepped outside. He saw an old man. A sick man. A dead body.
This happens to everyone, my prince. Even you.
That night, he left it all, even his wife and newborn son, to find out why we suffer, and how to stop.
For six years he barely ate, hoping it would bring answers. It almost killed him.
Then a woman named Sujata brought him rice and milk. He ate, and realised: starving wasn't the answer either.
So he sat under a tree at Bodh Gaya, and made a promise.
I will not get up until I understand.
By sunrise, he understood. We suffer because we always want more. Let go of that, and suffering ends.
From that day, people called him the Buddha: the one who woke up.
